findings.claim: When a `[MessagePackObject]` type declared in source inherits an unkeyed public field from a base class in a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 is now silently dropped. The guard at the changed line checks only `formattedType.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`, and `formattedType` here is the source type, so the diagnostic is still built. But `item` (the inherited field) comes from metadata, so `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()` gives a null location, i.e. `Location.None`. The new wrapper `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` (line 239, body at 1446) then throws the diagnostic away. The user's own source type gets no error for a public member that has neither `[Key]` nor `[IgnoreMember]` (L3), and nothing tells them the member is mishandled. Base crashed here (AD0001); head swaps the crash for a silent miss instead of reporting at a fallback location such as the derived type's identifier. The `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` path via `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` has the same gap for inherited metadata properties.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.InheritedMetadataMemberNeedsKeyTests.MemberNeedsKey_IsReported_ForPublicFieldInheritedFromReferencedAssembly. It compiles lib (`public class BaseType { public int Unkeyed; }`) to an image, references it from app (`[MessagePackObject] public class Derived : Lib.BaseType { [Key(0)] public int Keyed; }`), runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, and asserts that MsgPack004 is reported. On head no MsgPack004 is produced, so the test fails.
